chapter: Clubs, readers and musicians he knew
title: Scott Joplin, favorite numbers and which musicians could read
summary: Talk of Joplin orchestrations, Sonny Henry's reading, and bands like Piron's and Robichaux's that had readers.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: His band plays all the orchestrations, you know?
Yeah. I play the love band. Yeah. He plays all those, Scott Joplin. Yeah, you have the band parts too, eh? Yeah, right. Yeah. Scott Joplin. Scott Joplin, yeah, that was.
Did you ever play that kind of music?
Yeah, I used to like it too. It was real good.
What were some of your favorite numbers?
Well, I'll tell you the truth. I made them all favorites. You liked it, Mike. It's all good. Yeah, I tried to do everything well. You know, I liked it.
Yeah, he could read. Well, like I'm telling you, he wasn't a first class reader, but he read.
How many first class readers did you ever work with?

Oh, a few, like with Armand Pierron, they had a few in that band, and they had a few in Mr. Robichaud's band, worked with them, and I worked with a few others. Were you a regular member with Robichaud?
